speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Superdomains, Berezin integration, and Stokes boundaries
summary: The dated continuation begins on P000670, after a separate question about factors. Bernstein explains superfunctions, parity-preserving morphisms, nilpotent Taylor expansion, and why a boundary requires an embedded subsupermanifold in addition to its ordinary body. The circle and half-line examples lead to the Stokes problem, soon printed by Bernstein and Leites. P000673--P000674 explicitly form a retrospective summary of earlier super talks copied from I.~Dorfman's notebook; their definitions and linear algebra are indexed here with that provenance, rather than assigned a new seminar date. The catalogue's P000668--P000675 span also includes adjoining talks.

speaker: V. N. Popov [catalogue; attribution conflict]
title: Connections, free Yang--Mills fields, and Ricci-flat metrics
summary: The notes begin on P000675 with Gelfand's request for an elementary explanation of a connection and a reference to Yang and Mills. They develop gauge covariance, the principal-bundle equation \(H\delta_h\Phi=0\), its independence of the auxiliary vertical metric, and the affine-frame realization of the vacuum Einstein equations. The last two results match D.~A.~Popov's 1975 paper and D.~A.~Popov--L.~I.~Daikhin's 1975 note exactly. The supplied catalogue calls the speaker V.~N.~Popov, while the handwritten heading gives only Popov; that conflict is retained explicitly. Mathematical identification of the papers does not prove a correction of the speaker's initials. The identified notes occupy P000675--P000677, narrower than the catalogue's P000673--P000679 packet.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Euler products, compact-group heat kernels, and affine Lie algebras
summary: Bernstein explains Euler and Jacobi identities, Macdonald's root-system generalization, and Kostant's expression through characters and the Casimir. A shifted spectral zeta function is introduced, but its displayed reflection equation lacks the necessary Mellin completion. Olshanetsky intervenes on radial Laplacians and quantum integrability. Bernstein then gives the Cartan-matrix construction and the affine \(A_2\) loop-algebra example. The date 22 November is supplied by the catalogue; the corresponding handwritten start on P000678 is undated and P000680 ends with a New Year greeting. This evidence does not establish additional sessions within the packet. The mathematical notes are P000678--P000680, rather than the catalogue's wider P000677--P000681 span.

title: YEAR 1977

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Spectral curves, rank-two solitons, and filtered bimodules
summary: Manin begins with a reference to Calogero's boomeron, then describes a fourth-order Lax system and an explicitly singular, periodically oscillating rank-two pulse. The algebraic part passes from commuting operators to a spectral curve and eigenfunction bundles, contrasts rank-one Jacobian motion with higher-rank bundle moduli, and gives the filtered-bimodule construction and its inverse. Two further connections yield evolution and zero-curvature equations. The material has an unusually close later match in Manin's 1978 survey, including a sign error in the flatness formula that survives into the printed English translation. The last sentence announces Duistermaat for the next meeting; it does not contain that lecture.
